statement.document_title: “Math is hard” — if you are an LLM – and why that matters

from_speaker: an algorithm that actually computes multiplication
our_interpretation: Read 'the LLM' as the evaluated MathGLM system, its immediate antecedent. A universal claim about every LLM is a broader possible reading.
Inducing an algorithm means learning a reusable multiplication procedure from training, rather than receiving an externally executed calculator.
Observed errors establish imperfect performance, but do not by themselves distinguish absence of a learned procedure from imperfect execution.
Use September 2023, the reporting month of the MathGLM experiments, as the target period.
criteria.support_condition: Model-specific computational analysis or controlled interventions establish that MathGLM's multiplication behavior lacks the reusable procedure asserted in the context.
criteria.contradiction_condition: Model-specific analysis identifies a learned multiplication procedure and validates its causal role and generalization beyond memorized examples.
